concepts.name: Strait of Hormuz: Strategic and Geopolitical Significance
key_dimensions: Connects Persian Gulf to Gulf of Oman — NOT directly to Arabian Sea (common trap)
Countries it borders: Iran and Oman (UAE is nearby but does not directly border the strait)
Chokepoint status: ~20% of world's oil trade passes through it
Geopolitical flashpoints: Iran's threat to blockade and implications for global energy security

concepts.name: Strait of Malacca: Trade and Maritime Importance
key_dimensions: Connects Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) to South China Sea (Pacific Ocean)
Bordered by Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia — NOT Thailand directly
Busiest shipping lane in the world; handles ~25% of global trade
Piracy hotspot and China's 'Malacca Dilemma' — strategic vulnerability

concepts.name: Bab-el-Mandeb Strait: Red Sea Gateway
key_dimensions: Connects Red Sea to Gulf of Aden — gateway to Suez Canal route
Bordered by Yemen (Asia side) and Djibouti/Eritrea (Africa side)
Name means 'Gate of Grief/Tears' — historical and linguistic fact often asked
Houthi attacks (2023–24) disrupted global shipping — current affairs linkage

concepts.name: Strait of Gibraltar: Atlantic-Mediterranean Junction
key_dimensions: Connects Atlantic Ocean to Mediterranean Sea
Bordered by Spain (Europe) and Morocco (Africa) — UK controls Gibraltar (sovereignty dispute)
Pillars of Hercules — classical reference often used in prelims
Narrowest point (~14 km) and its significance for NATO naval strategy

concepts.name: Strait of Magellan vs. Drake Passage: Southern Tip of South America
key_dimensions: Strait of Magellan: separates mainland South America from Tierra del Fuego — sheltered route
Drake Passage: between Cape Horn (South America) and South Shetland Islands (Antarctica) — open ocean, not a strait technically
Both connect Atlantic and Pacific Oceans — but Drake is wider and rougher
Panama Canal made both strategically less critical — comparative question trap

concepts.name: Bering Strait: Asia-America Separation and Climate Significance
key_dimensions: Connects Arctic Ocean (Chukchi Sea) to Pacific Ocean (Bering Sea)
Separates Russia (Asia) from USA (Alaska) — narrowest point ~85 km
Land bridge theory: Beringia — human migration from Asia to Americas
Arctic shipping route viability with melting ice — NSR (Northern Sea Route) implications

concepts.name: Palk Strait and Palk Bay vs. Gulf of Mannar: India-Sri Lanka Waters
key_dimensions: Palk Strait: between Tamil Nadu and Northern Sri Lanka — shallow, not navigable by large ships
Gulf of Mannar: south of Palk Bay, between India and Sri Lanka — deeper, rich in marine biodiversity
Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu): chain of limestone shoals connecting India and Sri Lanka within Palk Strait
SETR (Sethusamudram Shipping Channel Project) — proposed canal through Palk Strait, controversies

concepts.name: Strait of Dover: Narrowest Point of English Channel
key_dimensions: Connects North Sea to English Channel — separates UK from France
Narrowest point (~33 km) — busiest shipping lane in the world by vessel count
Channel Tunnel (Chunnel) runs beneath it — engineering geography
Post-Brexit implications for maritime boundaries and fishing rights

concepts.name: Turkish Straits: Bosphorus and Dardanelles
key_dimensions: Bosphorus: connects Black Sea to Sea of Marmara; Dardanelles: connects Sea of Marmara to Aegean Sea
Together they are the only outlet from Black Sea to Mediterranean — controlled entirely by Turkey
Montreux Convention (1936): regulates naval passage — restricts warships of non-Black Sea nations
Russia-Ukraine war (2022): Ukraine requested Turkey to close straits to Russian warships — geopolitical trap

concepts.name: Lombok Strait and Sunda Strait: Indonesia's Strategic Alternatives
key_dimensions: Sunda Strait: between Sumatra and Java — alternative to Malacca for shallower vessels
Lombok Strait: between Bali and Lombok islands — deeper, preferred by large naval vessels and supertankers
Both are alternatives to Strait of Malacca — 'Lombok Alternative' in naval strategy
Krakatoa volcano located in Sunda Strait — physical geography linkage

concepts.name: Hudson Bay and Hudson Strait: Canada's Inland Sea
key_dimensions: Hudson Bay: large body of water in northeastern Canada — almost entirely surrounded by land (semi-enclosed sea, NOT a strait)
Hudson Strait: connects Hudson Bay to Labrador Sea (Atlantic Ocean)
Seasonal ice cover and its role in Arctic shipping discussions
Common trap: Hudson Bay is often confused with a bay in the traditional sense — it drains into Atlantic, not Pacific

concepts.name: Bay of Bengal vs. Arabian Sea: Comparative Physical Geography
key_dimensions: Bay of Bengal: bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand — eastern arm of Indian Ocean
Arabian Sea: bordered by India, Pakistan, Oman, Yemen, Somalia — western arm
Bay of Bengal receives more river discharge (Ganga-Brahmaputra-Irrawaddy) making it less saline
Cyclone frequency: Bay of Bengal has ~80% of world's tropical cyclones — warm, shallow waters reason

concepts.name: Gulf of Aden and Somali Piracy Corridor
key_dimensions: Connects Red Sea (via Bab-el-Mandeb) to Arabian Sea — critical Suez Canal feeder route
Bordered by Yemen (north) and Somalia/Djibouti (south)
Somali piracy peak (2008–2012) — EUNAVFOR Operation Atalanta, India's INS deployments
Distinction from Gulf of Oman: Gulf of Oman is further east, connects to Strait of Hormuz

concepts.name: Khyber Pass and Other Mountain Passes: Strategic Land Routes
key_dimensions: Khyber Pass: connects Pakistan (Peshawar) to Afghanistan (Kabul) through Hindu Kush — NOT Himalayas (common trap)
Nathu La Pass: Sikkim — India-China trade route, reopened in 2006
Bolan Pass: Pakistan — connects Quetta to Sibi through Balochistan
Zoji La: Jammu & Kashmir — connects Srinagar to Leh; strategic for Indian Army supply

concepts.name: Passes in the Himalayas and India's Strategic Mountain Passes
key_dimensions: Shipki La: Himachal Pradesh — India-China border; Sutlej River enters India through this pass
Lipulekh Pass: Uttarakhand — India-China-Nepal tri-junction, disputed by Nepal (2020 controversy)
Rohtang Pass vs. Atal Tunnel: Rohtang connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti; tunnel bypasses it
Jelep La: Sikkim — historic trade route, currently not operational for trade

concepts.name: Strait of Messina and Mediterranean Micro-Straits
key_dimensions: Strait of Messina: separates Sicily from mainland Italy (Calabria) — connects Tyrrhenian Sea to Ionian Sea
Mythological reference: Scylla and Charybdis (Homer's Odyssey) — located here
Planned Messina Bridge — world's longest suspension bridge proposal
Distinction from Strait of Otranto: connects Adriatic Sea to Ionian Sea, between Italy and Albania

concepts.name: Gulf of Mexico vs. Caribbean Sea: Boundary and Significance
key_dimensions: Gulf of Mexico: semi-enclosed sea bordered by USA, Mexico, Cuba — connected to Atlantic via Florida Straits
Florida Strait: between Florida (USA) and Cuba — connects Gulf of Mexico to Atlantic Ocean
Gulf of Mexico: major oil and gas reserves — Deepwater Horizon disaster (2010) linkage
Caribbean Sea: east of Central America — NOT the same as Gulf of Mexico (common confusion in prelims)

concepts.name: Mozambique Channel and Southern African Maritime Geography
key_dimensions: Separates Madagascar from mainland Africa (Mozambique) — part of Indian Ocean
One of the world's widest channels (~400 km at narrowest) — sometimes classified as a strait
Strategic importance: oil tanker route from Middle East to Europe around Cape of Good Hope
Rich fishing grounds and nascent offshore gas reserves — geopolitical competition

concepts.name: Taiwan Strait: Geopolitical Flashpoint
key_dimensions: Connects East China Sea to South China Sea — separates Taiwan from mainland China (Fujian province)
Width: ~180 km — US Navy routinely conducts 'freedom of navigation' operations here
China's claim that it is 'internal waters' vs. international law (UNCLOS) — legal geography trap
Strategic implications for Japan, South Korea, and India if strait is blocked

concepts.name: Cook Strait and Bass Strait: Southern Hemisphere Island Straits
key_dimensions: Cook Strait: separates North Island from South Island of New Zealand — connects Tasman Sea to South Pacific
Bass Strait: separates Tasmania from mainland Australia — connects Indian Ocean to Tasman Sea
Both are significant for Southern Ocean weather patterns and shipping
Common trap: Cook Strait is named after Captain James Cook — also explored Australian east coast
